clue.text: Boldness of a superior daughter coming to a place like London

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for upper-class or superior
London is an example of a city

explanation.surface: Someone from a posh family arrives in the capital and shows remarkable nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Audacity is a synonym for boldness, a daring willingness to take risks.

clue.text: Notice wickedness — provide counsel

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
vice means immorality or wickedness

explanation.surface: Someone spots wrongdoing and offers guidance about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice and counsel are synonyms: both are guidance offered on what to do.

clue.text: Periods restricting the Spanish — times when things don't get going

definitions.text: times when things don't get going

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: days are periods of time
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Holiday periods in Spain are times when nothing gets started.
explanation.definitionFit: Delays are hold-ups, occasions when progress is stalled and things fail to start.

clue.text: Study potential source of future energy? It's a mess

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
nuclear fusion is hoped to provide clean power someday

explanation.surface: Researching a possible energy source of tomorrow turns out to be chaotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Confusion is disorder or muddle, a state that can be called a mess.

clue.text: She slurped port — inappropriate for a holy meal

indicators.note: inappropriate suggests the letters are improperly placed, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman noisily gulps fortified wine, behaviour unsuited to a sacred meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord's Supper is the Christian sacrament of Holy Communion, commemorating Christ's last meal.

clue.text: Optical instruments in cloak smuggled aboard ship

indicators.note: something smuggled aboard a vessel ends up within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a cope is a long cloak worn by clergy

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks telescopes onto a ship hidden inside a cloak.
explanation.walkthrough: A cope is an ecclesiastical cloak; SS is the usual crossword ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Telescopes, microscopes and periscopes are all optical viewing instruments, informally called scopes.

clue.text: Food from what is harvested is not zero quantity

indicators.note: is not zero says the word is takes the place of the zero letter

parts.note: a crop is what is harvested
zero is the letter O

explanation.surface: Food from the harvest is not a negligible amount.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'is not zero' as IS where O was: CROP becomes CRISP.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp is a thin fried potato slice, a snack food (a chip in America).

clue.text: Part of country giving Cable support?

parts.note: pro means in favour of, giving support
Vince Cable is a British politician, former Liberal Democrat leader

explanation.surface: A region of the country that backs a cable line?
explanation.walkthrough: Vince Cable led Britain's Liberal Democrats; being 'pro-Vince' is giving him support.
explanation.definitionFit: A province is an administrative region or division of a country.

clue.text: Anticipation of wisdom keeping us quiet

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sense means good judgement or wisdom
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Waiting for some wise words keeps everyone silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the tense, uncertain state of waiting for something to happen.

clue.text: Man on board, first person to introduce a certain retaliatory action

parts.note: a counter is a piece, or man, in a board game
me is the first person pronoun
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A chess piece and a player introduce a definite move in retaliation.
explanation.definitionFit: A countermeasure is an action taken in response to counteract a threat.

clue.text: Very small church in which man's placed decorative material

indicators.note: the man is placed within the church letters, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: very is abbreviated to a small letter v
CE stands for Church of England
man's reads as man is; Alan is a man's name

explanation.surface: A tiny chapel where a man has hung some ornamental fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very small' is the lowercase v used as the abbreviation for very; 'placed' sets the man's name inside the church letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A valance is a decorative drapery hung along the edge of a bed, shelf or curtain rail.

clue.text: Sinister old male, one we heard in Paris

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
the French word for we, as spoken in Paris, is nous

explanation.surface: A creepy elderly man is someone we hear about while visiting Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ominous threatens harm, giving it a menacing, sinister quality.

clue.text: Rodent turning up, timid at first

indicators.note: tells us the timid piece comes at the start, before the other part

parts.note: coy means shy or timid

indicators.note: turning means the word up is read backwards

explanation.surface: A rodent shows up, shy at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American water rodent, also called nutria.

clue.text: New hotel I open, wasting little time — suits the wine connoisseur

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made into something fresh, a rearrangement
wasting means losing, so a letter is taken away from the hotel letters

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A new hotel opens in a hurry, which pleases the visiting wine expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting little time' removes T from HOTEL, leaving HOEL; 'New' shuffles HOEL, I and OPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An oenophile is a lover and connoisseur of wines, from Greek roots for wine and loving.

clue.text: Instrument won't shift rubbish!

parts.note: a fiddle is a violin, a musical instrument
something that sticks stays put and won't move

explanation.surface: Someone's instrument has jammed and they curse it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddlesticks is an old-fashioned exclamation meaning nonsense, like crying rubbish.

clue.text: Messing around with money, one monarch entertaining another

parts.note: tin is slang for money

indicators.note: entertaining a guest means having them inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a king is a monarch
another monarch: ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Fiddling with cash while one ruler plays host to another.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinkering means fiddling or meddling with something in an unskilled way.

clue.text: Mum and other women getting ailments

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
ladies are women

explanation.surface: Mother and some other women are falling ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladies are illnesses or disorders, synonyms for ailments.

clue.text: This writer's one contributing to blog, a fraud

parts.note: this writer is the setter, so this writer's means I'm, I am
a poster is one who posts to a blog or forum

explanation.surface: The setter confesses that their blog contributor is a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposter is someone who pretends to be another person to deceive, a fraud.

clue.text: Rebuke from nan, mixed up with Methodism

indicators.note: mixed up means jumbled, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Grandma gets a telling-off for confusing her religion with Methodism.
explanation.definitionFit: An admonishment is a reprimand, a stern word of warning or rebuke.

clue.text: European artist being held up inside gets temporary release

indicators.note: inside places the artist within the European

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland

indicators.note: held up in a down clue means the letters are lifted and read backwards

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A European painter held up in prison is let out for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Parole is the conditional early release of a prisoner for a period.

clue.text: Reproductive organ set man apart

indicators.note: apart means broken into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's reproductive organs set him apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the male, pollen-producing reproductive organ of a flower.

clue.text: Set of religious books that could make chap pray, having hidden love

indicators.note: having hidden means holding something concealed inside
could make says these letters could be fashioned into something else, a rearrangement

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Holy books could get a fellow praying while he keeps his feelings secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' gives APCRYPHA, eight shuffled letters; 'having hidden' tucks love's O into them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are biblical writings excluded from the Hebrew canon, printed as a separate group in some Bibles.

clue.text: Approach bringing disagreement

definitions.meaning: the run-up or final lead-up to an event
a quarrel or clash, especially with the authorities

explanation.surface: An approach that brings about an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is both the approach leading to something and an argument or clash.

clue.text: Accurate performance by one who has been discarded?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, someone dropped
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A routine performed by a former lover is spot on.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precise or correct in every detail, so it matches accurate.

clue.text: Feverish home has to confront future maybe

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
the future is one grammatical tense

explanation.surface: Someone at home has to face what lies ahead and is getting worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish activity is frenzied and intense, carried out with great energy.

clue.text: Even reluctant pupils may be forced to wear it

definitions.meaning: even means consistent, the same throughout

definitions.text: reluctant pupils may be forced to wear it
definitions.meaning: school pupils are often required to wear standard school clothing

explanation.surface: Even unwilling schoolchildren have to put on a certain outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform means unvarying and even; it is also the standard outfit worn at many schools.

clue.text: Problem for Henry King in train

definitions.meaning: in Hilaire Belloc's cautionary verse, Henry King died from chewing little bits of cord
a train is a series or line of things following one another

explanation.surface: A man called Henry King has trouble aboard a train.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry King is the boy in Hilaire Belloc's comic Cautionary Tales whose 'chief defect' was chewing string; British readers know it from school.
explanation.definitionFit: A string is a sequence or train of things; string was also Henry King's fatal habit.

clue.text: Colour of enclosure encompassing match

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
to match is to correspond or agree

explanation.surface: The colour of a fenced field surrounding a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea green is a bright yellowish-green shade, the colour of fresh peas.
